flows.narrative: The latest confirmed BofA Flow Show (week ended 23 Sep) showed a sharp reversal from risk-on: US equity funds lost $21.1bn and global equity funds lost $10.2bn (vs +$63.8bn the week before), while fixed income extended its inflow streak to 74 straight weeks (+$17.3bn) and the Bull & Bear Indicator sat at 9.3, still deep in the contrarian 'Sell' zone. ICI's own weekly print for the same week (confirmed live from ici.org) tells a more nuanced story: combined long-term fund + ETF flows were actually +$20.14bn, as a +$39.81bn ETF net issuance more than offset a -$19.67bn long-term mutual fund outflow -- both trackers agree flows reversed sharply from the prior week, but ICI's ETF-inclusive combined figure is less negative than BofA's fund-flow-only read. Gold's picture is muddier: global gold ETFs are on an 8-week, ~$20bn inflow streak through August, but SPDR Gold Shares (GLD) itself saw a $603m weekly redemption around week ended 12 Sep that was largely a fee-driven rotation into lower-cost GLDM/IAU/IAUM rather than an exit from gold overall.
